headline: pki.cmp.session drives a full CMP certificate enrollment end to end -- build, transfer, and verify every leg of an ir/cr/kur/p10cr exchange, with every response protection-checked before its body is read.
summary: The Certificate Management Protocol surface gains its stateful client. pki.cmp.session(opts) is the enrollment-transaction orchestrator that composes the shipped message layer (pki.cmp.build / transfer / verify) into a single call: session.enroll(request) runs an RFC 9810 enrollment (ir, cr, kur, or p10cr) to completion over an injectable transport (or a fail-closed HTTPS transport). It mints one stable 128-bit transactionID for the whole exchange and a fresh senderNonce per request, echoing the peer's last senderNonce back as recipNonce so a response cannot be replayed or interleaved into the transaction (RFC 9810 sec. 5.1.1). The load-bearing rule is transfer then verify then read: every response's protection is verified and bound to this exchange BEFORE any field of its body is acted on, so a meddler who flips an HTTP response cannot forge a granted status or a poisoned poll delay -- a tampered, unverifiable, or desynchronized response is a hard-stop throw, never a certificate the caller can misread. Crypto-valid protection is not sufficient: the response signer must chain to a supplied trust anchor (signature) or the shared secret must match (MAC), and a valid-but-untrusted signer is a hard stop -- so the signature flavor requires a trust anchor at construction. A waiting status drives a bounded pollReq/pollRep loop (an injectable sleeper, capped by a poll count and a total-wait budget, so a CA cannot hold the client indefinitely); a grant extracts the issued certificate and confirms it with a certConf/pkiConf handshake unless implicit confirmation was granted -- detected from the granting response's own header, including when the grant arrives after polling. The certConf certHash uses the issued certificate's signature hash, declaring an explicit hashAlg when the algorithm (RSASSA-PSS, Ed25519/Ed448, ML-DSA) does not convey it, and the caller's CRMF certReqId is echoed in every pollReq/certConf and matched in each response. A verified rejection or error, or a poll-budget timeout, is a terminal typed verdict the caller reads (outcome: issued, rejected, or poll-timeout) rather than a throw. Protection is exactly one flavor: a signing key and certificate, or a PBMAC1 shared secret; both drive the identical transaction. RFC 9810 sec. 5.1.1 / 5.2.3 / 5.3.4 / 5.3.18 / 5.3.22, RFC 9811, RFC 9483.

Added: pki.cmp.session(opts) returns a stateful CMP enrollment session; session.enroll(request) drives an RFC 9810 ir / cr / kur / p10cr exchange to completion and returns a terminal verdict { outcome, certificate, chain, status, trusted, confirmed, implicitConfirm, transactionID, polls, transcript }. Every response is protection-verified (pki.cmp.verify) and bound to the transaction by transactionID and a fresh-senderNonce / echoed-recipNonce chain before its body is read, and is advanced only if its signer is trusted (chains to a supplied anchor, or the shared secret matches); a waiting status is polled under a bounded pollReq/pollRep loop; a grant is confirmed by a certConf/pkiConf handshake unless implicit confirmation was granted. opts.key + opts.cert select signature protection (with opts.trustAnchors REQUIRED to authenticate the CA's response signer, opts.intermediates an extra chain pool) or opts.mac selects PBMAC1; opts.transport / opts.tls / opts.timeout / opts.maxResponseBytes configure transfer; opts.maxPolls / opts.maxTotalWait / opts.sleep bound the poll loop; opts.sender / opts.recipient / opts.implicitConfirm / opts.extraCerts tune the request. A verified rejection or error, or an exhausted poll budget, is a terminal outcome; a tampered, unverifiable, untrusted, or nonce-mismatched response is a typed CmpError throw. RFC 9810 sec. 5.1.1 / 5.2.3 / 5.3.4 / 5.3.18 / 5.3.22, RFC 9811, RFC 9483.
